description:
New align type: 'left-right' for options.scales['x'].ticks namespace will allow users to aling horizontal axis ticks: 'start" for first (left) tick and 'end' for last (right) tick.
Before:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50024798/151367440-e4c637ea-ddaa-4072-95a3-991b7e016469.png)

After:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50024798/151367611-3b20ee96-d89e-4005-8dde-92d0c65723f2.png)

comments.body:
Might be a better idea to change this to an else if block, check if it is the last tick then change the alignment. This way you can change the name of alignment to `inner` for example so all ticks align within the chart area. 

This way if you want you outer ticks to be inside but the others (if you have them) nicely centered that also still works. Makes it a bit more flexible
How will this work when labels are rotated on a horizontal axis? It might be better to disable this in that case.
In general we've tried to keep the public facing options direction agnostic (i.e. 'start' instead of 'left'). Perhaps this could be named `'auto'`?
This alligment doesn`t affect rotated labels. Add a image based test for this case
I like suggestion from LeeLenaleee and renamed this alligment type to "inner"
Thanks for suggestions! Very good idea!
Would remove this, since it only applies to horizontal axes this will give confusion

Old one was correct, you only changed the alignment for the ticks in the axis, this type is used for a lot of other parts where it does not apply

```suggestion
export type TextAlign = 'left' | 'center' | 'right';
```
This made me think what happens if the scale is reversed?

Alignment also needs to be flipped in that case: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39033624/152689397-613901d4-b60c-424b-a81e-15e4b1503c39.png)
Thanks for this case investigation) Correct logic for reverse axis and add additional test

Align already has the `'start' | 'center' | 'end'` in it, so would be cleaner if it was just
```suggestion
    align: Align | 'inner';
```

For the rest looks good
